links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT vs LexiComp patient education materials
links.effect: Reading level was higher with ChatGPT [8.6 (1.2) vs. 5.6 (0.3), P < 0.001); ChatGPT PEMs did not meet grade level targets.
links.quote: Reading level was higher with ChatGPT [8.6 (1.2) vs. 5.6 (0.3), P < 0.001).

links.outcome: Understandability (PEMAT-P) and readability of ChatGPT patient education materials versus LexiComp
links.effect: PEMAT-P understandability did not differ (77.9% vs 72.5%, P=0.193), but reading grade level was higher (8.6 vs 5.6, P<0.001); fewer passive sentences and lower word count.
links.quote: No difference was found in the PEMAT-P understandability score of PEMs produced by ChatGPT versus LexiComp® [77.9% (11.0) vs. 72.5% (2.4), P=0.193].

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT medication education materials on 7-item expert checklist
links.effect: Average accuracy score of ChatGPT PEMs was 4.25/7 (61%), ranging from 29% to 86%.
links.quote: The average accuracy score of ChatGPT PEMs was 4.25/7 (61%), with scores ranging from 29% to 86%.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, readability, and understandability of ChatGPT-generated patient education materials compared to a standard drug database (LexiComp), without testing a deployment safeguard or practice.
